children: Italy's trade surplus widened to €8.24 billion in July 2026, the largest since July 2020, from €7.83 billion in July 2025 and well above market forecasts of €4.77 billion.

Exports grew by 4.7% yoy to a record high of €64.55 billion, bolstered by shipments of basic metals and fabricated metal products (+13.8%), coke and refined petroleum products (+27.3%), and sporting goods, games, musical instruments, precious metals, medical instruments, and others (+15.9%).
Overseas sales grew more strongly for non-EU markets (+6.6%), particularly Switzerland (+39.6%), followed by OPEC countries (+26.3%) and China (+27.6%).
Exports to the EU increased 2.8%, led by the Netherlands (+5%) and France (+4.2%).
Meanwhile, imports rose by 4.6% to €56.31 billion, driven by mining & quarrying (28.7%); coke and refined petroleum products (+27%) and basic metals and fabricated metal products (+9.9%).
Imports from EU and non-EU countries rose by 4.9% and 4.2%, respectively.

title: Italy Posts Widest Trade Surplus in 6 Years
